segments: the structure of the stones of Bar Hebraeus {OCR?}... And then the king of England set out,
and took Cyprus from the Greeks,
and came and encamped against Acre.
And the Franks were greatly emboldened by his coming.
Inside, however, there were twenty emirs of the Arabs (Muslims),
and they sent word and said to Saladin:
"We have already been weakened and enfeebled by the constant fighting,
and sickness also afflicts us."
So Saladin gave command, and they went out from the sea side,
and in their place he brought in others.
And because these were not skilled in fighting upon the wall,
the Franks gained greater mastery,
and they set up seven mangonels against a single tower.
And the king of England sent an envoy to Saladin and said:
"It is not harmful if I and you sit in one place
and make an arrangement that is profitable to both sides."
Saladin, however, replied:
"First an arrangement of peace must be established,
and afterward a meeting together;
because after conversation and banquet,
warfare is not seemly."
And in those days that king of England fell sick with a severe sickness,
and the Franks slackened from the fight because of his sickness.
And when he recovered,
he again sent an envoy to Saladin and said:
"Do not complain that my communication with you was cut off,
because sickness hindered me;
and now I have recovered,
and I have sent to you that, if you permit, I might send you gifts.
For it is not right for kings to cut off gifts and embassies and words of love from one another,
even though war is waged between them.
For so the laws of our ancestors, the ancient kings, teach us."
And Saladin replied:
"Very well,
if you accept from us in return for your gifts,
we will accept gifts from you."
And the envoy said:
"We have falcons, eagles, and other predatory birds,
and they have grown weak.
And we ask that you give us (hens? hens:
hens) and pigeons,
that we may nourish them so that they grow strong,
and we will bring them to you."

And al-Malik al-Adil, Saladin's brother, while cheering up... [Bedjan's note:] The king of Anglitar, or of Anglitr? Or of Englis, or of Engelterra? We everywhere write "the king of England (Engelterra)",
for in our time that country is called in the East Englis or Engelterra.
notes: 4) Richard: who because of his great courage was called the Lion Heart.
